Advances: specled.api_boundary

Review-bar-override: scoping the block changes what specled.api_boundary.divergence_blocks_refresh currently requires — needs a spec amendment + ADR.

From the critical review of specled_-n5q (finding F29, Medium, consensus: security + api).

has_divergence?/1 is a whole-run boolean applied to a refresh that rewrites every flat tier, so one stuck api_boundary MFA freezes rebaselining for expanded_behavior, typespecs, and use. The attestation path already has the granularity this path lacks — drift_dangling_pairs/1 scopes to subject_id + mfa.

This is consistent with how has_drift?/has_dangling? already behave, so it is not a design objection — the scope is simply undocumented and an adopter debugging a stale unrelated tier will not connect it.

The documentation half LANDED on the release branch (docs/concepts.md now states the block is run-wide and that severity off suppresses the report but not the block). This ticket is the behavioral half only.

## ORCHESTRATOR CONTRACT (specled_-i4x)

Advances: specled.api_boundary

BLOCKED BY specled_-vzd.4. That ticket introduces finding_code/1 + has_code?/2 + the
@drift_code/@dangling_code/@divergence_code attributes and renames drift_dangling_pairs/1. If
this ticket landed first it would write a FIFTH inline `Map.get(f, "code") || Map.get(f, :code)`
copy that vzd.4 then folds in, and vzd.4's rename would land on a function this ticket just
reshaped — a guaranteed same-hunk conflict. After vzd.4, this ticket reduces to an additive
extractor composed from has_code?/2.

DECISION-CLASS: code + spec amendment + ADR, but MERGEABLE after routine review — not held.
The amendment narrows specled.api_boundary.divergence_blocks_refresh
(.spec/specs/api_boundary.spec.md:109-119) and its scenario at :224-233 from run-wide to
per-MFA. change_type: narrows-scope. No weakening class fires (no deletion, no modal downgrade,
no scenario-count drop, no polarity loss), so the weakened-id set is empty and
append_only/same_pr_self_authorization cannot fire. The ADR is required by convention and
specled.decisions.frontmatter_contract, not by a gate.

Allowed touches:
- lib/specled_ex/realization/orchestrator.ex
- .spec/specs/api_boundary.spec.md
- .spec/decisions/specled.decision.*.md  (one new ADR, change_type: narrows-scope)
- test/specled_ex/realization/orchestrator_test.exs
- test/specled_ex/realization/api_boundary_test.exs
- .spec/specs/branch_guard.spec.md  (surface owner of orchestrator.ex, branch_guard.spec.md:24)
- docs/concepts.md AND .spec/specs/package.spec.md — CORRECTION ONLY, and MANDATORY: the
  documentation half of this finding already landed at docs/concepts.md:336-347. If this ticket
  lands, lines 336-341 ("The block spans the whole run, not just the diverged entry") BECOME
  FALSE and must be corrected in the same PR.
- .spec/realization_hashes.json  (escape hatch only)

Out of Scope (files):
- lib/specled_ex/realization/api_boundary.ex
- all other realization modules

Out of Scope (intent):
- Do NOT scope has_drift?/1 or has_dangling?/1 (orchestrator.ex:686-701). They are run-wide by
  design and the ticket says so. The resulting asymmetry (divergence per-MFA, drift run-wide) is
  a deliberate accepted consequence — put it in the ADR's Consequences section, not the diff.
- Do not change what --accept-drift does.
- Do not rename drift_dangling_pairs/1 — that is vzd.4 item 3, which lands before you.
- Do not merge the entry_hash/1 decode duplication (api_boundary.ex:191-201). It is consumed at
  :120 inside the same cond your divergence logic feeds, so it looks adjacent and inviting. It
  is vzd.4 item 1.

PRECISION POINT THE ADR MUST STATE: refresh_and_commit_hashes/3 (orchestrator.ex:897-920) builds
a TIER -> MFA map, while drift_dangling_pairs/1 (:396-414) yields {subject_id, mfa}. The store
has NO subject dimension, so the achievable exclusion granularity is {tier, mfa}, NOT
{subject_id, mfa}. Two subjects binding the same MFA with one diverged means excluded for both.
Say so explicitly; do not claim a granularity the store cannot express.

Verification:
  mix compile --warnings-as-errors
  mix test test/specled_ex/realization/orchestrator_test.exs test/specled_ex/realization/api_boundary_test.exs
  mix test --only spec:specled.api_boundary.divergence_blocks_refresh
  mix test --only spec:specled.api_boundary.divergence_withholds_drift_silencing
  mix format --check-formatted
  make xref
  bash ./scripts/check_specs.sh
NO stub flip: all four tagged_tests blocks in api_boundary.spec.md are already execute: true,
and orchestrator_test.exs already carries
@tag spec: "specled.api_boundary.divergence_blocks_refresh".

Expected diff: 5-6 files, ~220 lines.

With that assertion neutralized, the cross-tier assertion at :1674 — `refute Map.has_key?(fetch_entry(store, "expanded_behavior", clean_mfa), "stale_marker")` — fires independently, so BOTH the same-tier and other-tier halves of the permissive claim are live, not one masking the other.

Killed at :1664 — `assert fetch_entry(store, "api_boundary", diverged_mfa)["resolved_via"] == "source"` (left: "beam"); :1667 hash-equality would also catch it. The restrictive/safety half is pinned, not just the permissive half.
- Observes the WRITTEN baseline: yes. Every assertion reads `HashStore.read(root)`, which reads `<root>/.spec/realization_hashes.json` off disk; nothing is asserted off an in-memory return. The vzd.4 seed/refresh masking does NOT apply: all four observed entries are pre-committed by `HashStore.write(root, seeded)` before the run, and `seed_uncommitted_hashes/3` (orchestrator.ex:739) only computes hashes for bindings absent from the committed store — so seed provably cannot be the writer of any observed value. The `stale_marker`/`resolved_via` sentinels only disappear/appear via the refresh path.
- {tier, mfa} coarseness (two subjects sharing a diverged MFA both frozen): UNPINNED by any test — no test in the repo binds one MFA from two subjects in a divergence scenario. Mutant 3 (exclusion re-keyed to {tier, subject_id, mfa}, exactly the "improvement" the ADR forbids) passes GREEN across all 50 tests. BUT I probed the scenario directly and it is behaviorally unobservable: divergence is a property of the stored entry, not of the subject, so every subject binding the same {tier, mfa} emits its own divergence finding (probe with two subjects returned subject_ids ["a.subject", "b.subject"]), and divergence findings are not `inferred?`-suppressed the way dangling findings are (api_boundary.ex:144, :232). Under subject-scoped code the shared entry still stays frozen for both. So the ADR limit is a true consequence of the store shape that no implementation can violate — an untestable statement, not an unguarded one. Reported as required; not scored against the ticket.
- Additional unpinned dimension found: mutant 5 (tier-blind exclusion — key by mfa only, ignoring tier) also passes GREEN. The amended must and the ADR both say `(tier, mfa)`; a tier-blind implementation would silently over-freeze an MFA's entries in the other flat tiers. Unlike the coarseness above this IS observable and cheap to pin: bind `diverged_mfa` under `expanded_behavior` as well and assert that entry DOES refresh. Low severity (needs one MFA bound in two tiers), recorded as a follow-up, not a blocker.
- --accept-drift still covered and unchanged: covered by test/integration/drift_acceptance_test.exs (5 tests), which this diff does not touch and which passes at HEAD. Its test at :227 pins the exact combination the new `refresh_allowed?` preserves as a run-wide block (divergence + same-path drift + --accept-drift → no refresh, no `info` downgrade). Mutant 6 (drop the new `not (has_drift? and has_divergence?)` sub-term) turns it RED at :300 "no baseline may move on a diverged run". Truth-table check of old vs new gate: identical in every combination that does not involve divergence.
- Attestation path scoping not conflated with refresh scoping: `unattested_pairs/1` (orchestrator.ex:410, called at :264) is untouched by the diff and still keys `{subject_id, mfa}`. The test keeps the two observations in separate assertions with separate sources — attestation via the returned `%{subject_id => %{path => {:attested_clean, mfas}}}` map (:1680-1686), refresh via the on-disk store (:1662-1677). No assertion crosses them.
- Expanding an existing test did not weaken its prior assertions: all five prior assertions survive verbatim in substance (divergence finding emitted; diverged `resolved_via` == "source"; diverged hash == seeded; divergence finding under --accept-drift; diverged hash unchanged under --accept-drift). The one rewritten assertion — `assert Map.get(attestations, "diverged.subject", %{}) == %{}` → `Map.fetch!` + `refute diverged_mfa in attested_mfas` — had to change because the subject now legitimately has a clean attesting sibling; the empty-bucket form would be false. `Map.fetch!` still raises if the bucket vanishes and the flat_map's `{_path, {:attested_clean, mfas}}` pattern still raises on any other shape, so the exclusion property is preserved. The added `HashStore.write(root, seeded)` reset between the two runs is required (run 1 relabels the clean entries) and does not touch the diverged-entry assertions.
- Sweep: no `Process.sleep` / `:timer.sleep` anywhere in the file. Per-test unique tmp root (`:erlang.unique_integer([:positive])`) with `on_exit(fn -> File.rm_rf!(root) end)`, so cleanup runs on failure too. `async: false` at module level is justified in-file (fixture module recompile/purge) and the per-test root rules out collision with the other 49 tests; adding two more tier/MFA entries introduces no shared state. Full file green: 50 tests, 0 failures.

Verdict rationale: both halves of the contract are pinned by independent, non-vacuous assertions read off the written baseline — the revert mutant and the over-correction mutant each die on a different assertion, which is exactly the pairing the calibration note asks for. The gap the ticket contract worried about (proving only the permissive half) is not present. The two unpinned dimensions are a spec limit that is structurally unfalsifiable and a low-severity tier-blindness that no realistic refactor path reaches; neither warrants blocking.

THE vzd.4 MASKING DOES NOT APPLY HERE, and that was worth checking explicitly: the sibling ticket's
regression test reads the post-refresh file, which hid a seed-only divergence. Here every observed
entry is pre-committed via HashStore.write before the run, and seed_uncommitted_hashes/3 only
computes hashes for bindings ABSENT from the committed store — so seeding provably cannot be the
writer of any observed value. All assertions read the on-disk baseline, not an in-memory return.

GRANULARITY HONESTY, the subtle failure mode on this ticket: neither the ADR nor the amended must
claims {subject_id, mfa}. Both state the store limit outright — "Because the hash store has no
subject dimension, the baseline shall not be refreshed for any subject sharing the diverged
(tier, mfa)" — and the ADR lists it under Consequences as a cost rather than hiding it.

TWO UNPINNED DIMENSIONS, neither blocking, with an important distinction between them:
1. The {tier, mfa} coarseness (two subjects sharing a diverged MFA both frozen) is unpinned by any

   The ADR's limit is a true consequence of the store shape that no implementation can violate — an
   untestable statement, not an unguarded one. Correctly not scored against the ticket.
2. TIER-BLINDNESS IS GENUINELY UNPINNED and IS observable. Keying the exclusion by mfa alone,
   ignoring tier, passes all 50 tests — yet the must and ADR both say (tier, mfa), and a tier-blind
   implementation would silently over-freeze an MFA's entries in the other flat tiers. Cheap to
   close: bind the diverged MFA under expanded_behavior too and assert that entry DOES refresh.

--accept-drift is unchanged and still covered by test/integration/drift_acceptance_test.exs, which

The attestation path is NOT conflated with the refresh path: unattested_pairs/1 is untouched and

Expanding an existing test rather than adding one did not weaken it: all five prior assertions
